question: Which of the following Vedas mentions the names of some learned ladies like Viswavara, Apala and Ghosa who composed mantras and attained the rank of Rishis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Rigveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest and most significant of the four Vedas, composed in Sanskrit and dating back to 1500-1200 BCE.
 
• It contains hymns dedicated to various deities and mentions learned women like Viswavara, Apala, and Ghosa, who composed hymns and attained the status of Rishis.
 
• These women were considered highly knowledgeable and contributed to spiritual and philosophical discourses during the Vedic period.
 
• The Rigveda highlights the active participation of women in intellectual and religious activities, showcasing their esteemed position in Vedic society.
 
• Viswavara, Apala, and Ghosa are notable examples of women who broke societal barriers and achieved recognition as composers of sacred mantras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Rigveda**:

 
 
• The Rigveda consists of 1,028 hymns organized into ten books called Mandalas.
 
• It is primarily a collection of praises to deities like Agni, Indra, Varuna, and others.
 
• Its language is an early form of Sanskrit, considered to be one of the oldest Indo-European languages.
 
 
 
• **Women in the Vedic Period**:
 
 
• Women in the Vedic age were actively involved in religious practices and philosophical discussions.
 
• They were allowed to participate in yajnas and educate themselves in sacred knowledge.
 
• Some women, like Gargi and Maitreyi, were also renowned for their philosophical contributions in later texts like the Upanishads.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Rishis**:
 
 
• Rishis were considered sages who composed hymns in praise of deities and imparted spiritual knowledge.
 
• The Vedas recognize both male and female Rishis, emphasizing gender equality in spiritual attainment.
 
 
 
• **Other Vedas**:
 
 
• The Samaveda is a collection of melodies and chants used in religious rituals.
 
• The Yajurveda consists of prose and mantras for performing sacrificial rituals.
 
• The Atharvaveda contains hymns, spells, and charms addressing everyday life and spiritual practices.
